clue.text: Top money for US chain

parts.note: a top performer is a star
bucks is slang for dollars, so money

explanation.surface: A query about the highest pay at an American chain of shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Starbucks is the American coffeehouse company with branches worldwide.

clue.text: Expulsion, rough stuff

definitions.meaning: coarse cloth such as hessian, used to make sacks

explanation.surface: Being thrown out described as a rough business.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the sack means dismissal, and the coarse fabric of sacks is also called sacking.

clue.text: Old student in compound before sunup

indicators.note: before puts the compound ahead of the next piece in the answer

parts.note: alum is a chemical compound, a double sulphate used in dyeing
read as sun up: in a down clue the word sun written upwards

explanation.surface: A former pupil found inside some building before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunup' looks like dawn, but split it as 'sun up': SUN read upwards gives NUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a graduate or former pupil of a school or college.

clue.text: Damn sexist filmed pinching the bottoms of Israeli and Filipino women

indicators.note: pinching means the film character's name grips the next word inside it

parts.note: Borat is the boorish, sexist character filmed by Sacha Baron Cohen

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of each word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a chauvinist on camera groping women from two countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'sexist filmed' is Borat, Sacha Baron Cohen's mock-documentary character; 'pinching' and 'bottoms' read as groping but are the containment and last-letter signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Botheration is a mild oath of annoyance, used just like the interjection damn.

clue.text: Horse carrying daughter and old man up — one of two runners?

indicators.note: carrying means the horse holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a colt is a young male horse

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for father is written upwards

parts.note: old man is slang for father, so pa

explanation.surface: A horse bearing a daughter and her father, apparently one of two racers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' suggests racehorses, but here it means taps, from which water runs; a basin usually has two.
explanation.definitionFit: A sink has a hot and a cold tap, and water runs from each, so either is a runner.

clue.text: It indicates the gang, I suspect, somewhat set up

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a gang has been framed and something points to it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' reads the hidden run upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Signage is the collection of signs, whose whole job is to point the way or show information.

clue.text: See 13
Brilliant books

definitions.meaning: ... means ... up, bright, or in slang excellent

explanation.surface: Praise for some excellent reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit means illuminated or, as slang, great; it also abbreviates literature, the written works.

clue.text: Wood: one saved by grant

indicators.note: saved by means the numeral is kept safe inside the verb for granting

parts.note: to confer is to grant or bestow
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Timber, with one person rescued by a financial award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grant' reads as a noun, a sum of money, but is the verb confer.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer is a cone-bearing tree such as pine, and its timber is a softwood.

clue.text: Legal body that's corrupt use suspect to stitch me up

indicators.note: to stitch up is to enclose by sewing round, so the shuffled letters close round the next piece
completes the phrase stitch up, enclosing the second piece
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A court is called corrupt for framing the speaker on a dodgy charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges CORRUPT USE as SUPRECOURT; 'to stitch ... up' sews ME into it. Stitch up looks like framing someone, but here it encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme court is the highest judicial body in a country, a legal institution.

clue.text: See 8
Relax, having forced in the plug

indicators.note: forced means the letters have been pushed out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Told to chill out after shoving a plug into a socket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' rearranges IN THE PLUG.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten up is an idiom meaning to stop being so serious and loosen up.

clue.text: Local news after one

indicators.note: after puts the second piece following the numeral in the answer

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
read as new's plural: N for new, twice

explanation.surface: Neighbourhood news arriving after one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for a neighbourhood pub, which an inn is; 'news' is read as two Ns, N being short for new.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain one's local is the nearby pub, and an inn is a pub.

clue.text: Can with ten free nuts, last of those going in tin?

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order
last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A tin can comes with ten free nuts, the last of the batch packed in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin' is British slang for money, so 'going in tin' is money for going in. 'nuts' rearranges CAN TEN FREE; E ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance fee is the charge for admission, the cash paid to get in.

clue.text: First of inspectors, people parting tidy hair — might they be on the case?

definitions.text: might they be on the case?

indicators.note: parting means the pieces separate the hair words, as a parting divides the hair

parts.note: to comb is to tidy hair
locks are tresses of hair

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Inspectors and people part someone's tidy hair, perhaps as detectives on a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the case' sounds like detectives, but these locks sit on a briefcase or safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Combination locks open with a code of numbers and are fitted to briefcases and safes.

clue.text: Blow into hole in burner

indicators.note: into means the blow goes inside the word for hole

parts.note: a gap is a hole or opening
a slam is a heavy blow

explanation.surface: Someone blows into a hole in a stove burner.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas lamp produces light by burning gas, so it is a kind of burner.

clue.text: Wood taking minutes instead of seconds in film studios

indicators.note: taking means the place adopts a new letter
instead of says one letter stands in for another

parts.note: Elstree is a town near London famous for its film studios

explanation.surface: Timber used in film studios, with a time unit swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Elstree is a British film-studio town north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An elm is a broadleaf tree whose timber is a hardwood, so it gives wood.

clue.text: Less clear, fade in drum beat

indicators.note: in places the word for fade inside the shuffled letters
beat means battered, so the letters of the word before are knocked into a new order

parts.note: to die away is to fade

explanation.surface: A drummer fades out to make the music murkier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like the drum's rhythm but is the anagram signal, giving MUDR around the inserted word.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddier water is cloudier, so less clear; ideas can be muddier too.

clue.text: Complain about noise coming from boozer, perhaps, punk style

indicators.note: about means the complaint wraps round the drunk's noise

parts.note: to moan is to complain
hic is the hiccup of a drunkard

explanation.surface: Grumbling about the racket from a pub, maybe from punks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' can be a British pub, but here it is a drunk who hiccups.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican is the haircut with a central strip of upright hair, typical of punks.

clue.text: Execute mythical king in US chain

parts.note: to do something is to execute it
Minos is the legendary king of Crete

explanation.surface: Putting a legendary king to death in an American franchise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execute' suggests killing, but it means carry out.
explanation.definitionFit: Domino's is the American pizza delivery chain.

clue.text: Accusation by theatre where fiddler played?

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
the musical is Fiddler on the Roof

explanation.surface: A charge brought by a theatre where a fiddler performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddler on the Roof' is the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke, a reproach for wrongdoing, which accuses.

clue.text: Broadcast about child ending in squalor — here?

indicators.note: about means the word for sowing goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it
a kid is a child

indicators.note: ending in takes the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A child's life on the news ending in poverty, perhaps right here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio, but it is scattering seed. 'here' means the place where one ends in squalor.
explanation.definitionFit: Skid row is the rundown district of vagrants and down-and-outs, where squalor lies.

clue.text: Loud speaker, improvisation of tenor underway?

parts.note: read as under way: the shuffled tenor sits under ST, the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: improvisation means the letters are played freely in a new order

explanation.surface: A singer improvising his tenor part as the show gets going, very loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underway' means getting started, but split it as 'under way': in a down answer the shuffled singer sits beneath the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was a herald in Homer with a huge voice, hence anyone very loud.

clue.text: Creator of famous solver given good position

parts.note: Ian Rankin created the Edinburgh detective Inspector Rebus

explanation.surface: The man behind a famous puzzle-solver landing a good post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solver' hints at crosswords, but it is Rankin's detective, John Rebus.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is a place in a graded order, a standing.

clue.text: US chain bringing up regulations on public transport?

indicators.note: bringing up means the whole phrase is read upwards in this down clue
on means the regulations follow the transport word, as in a rule applying to it

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle of public transport
law is the body of regulations

explanation.surface: An American retailer raising the rules for trams and buses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulations on public transport' is read as TRAM LAW, a law for trams; 'bringing up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Walmart is the huge American chain of discount department stores.

clue.text: Bees, perhaps, built honeytrap to trap me!

indicators.note: to trap means the rearranged letters catch the next word inside them
built means the letters are assembled afresh into a new structure

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a honey trap was set up to catch them, perhaps by bees.
explanation.walkthrough: A honeytrap is a seduction ploy, but here its letters are just fodder for 'built'; the definition 'Bees, perhaps' is an example of the insect order.
explanation.definitionFit: Hymenoptera is the insect order containing bees, wasps and ants, so bees are one example.

clue.text: Fastener lacking in a zip for Americans?

indicators.note: lacking means the following letter is missing from the fastener word

parts.note: a nail is a fastener

explanation.surface: An American zip without its fastening piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' looks like a zipper, but Americans use it for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is American slang for zero, and nil means nothing.

clue.text: Rocky, having struck bow in tilt — narrow vessel

indicators.note: in places the trimmed boxer inside the word for tilt

parts.note: cant is a slope or tilt

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a vessel, so striking it removes the first letter

parts.note: Rocky Balboa is the boxer played by Sylvester Stallone

explanation.surface: A boxer bowled over and tilting, like a narrow boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocky Balboa is the film boxer; losing his bow (front) leaves ALBOA.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal boat, such as a narrowboat, is a slim vessel built for canals.

clue.text: Place where cap knocked from toy

indicators.note: the cap of a down word is its top letter, so it is knocked off

parts.note: to play is to toy with

explanation.surface: A spot where a toy's cap got knocked off.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something is to set it down in position.

clue.text: Island where unknown character has broken bone, having struck head

indicators.note: has broken means the letter has burst into the bone
striking the head removes the first letter of the bone

parts.note: the tibia is the shinbone
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: On an island a mysterious figure breaks a bone after hitting their head.
explanation.walkthrough: TIBIA loses its head to leave IBIA, and 'has broken' puts Z inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish island in the Balearics.

clue.text: Refusal to admit someone good is bad

indicators.note: to admit means the refusal lets the next piece in

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
ST is short for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Refusing to let a good person in is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means unpleasant or wicked, a synonym of bad.

clue.text: Verbally, was jousting for some time

indicators.note: verbally means spoken out loud, so the phrase is said rather than spelt

parts.note: someone jousting fought a knight, said as fought knight

explanation.surface: A spoken claim of jousting for some while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was jousting' gives 'fought knight', which said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortnight is a period of two weeks, a length of time.
